walkthroughs.body_html:
The Changing Economic World — a core area of GCSE Geography.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

The Changing Economic World brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with The Changing Economic World.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

Glocalisation is a typo of globalisation.
It is the process of rain falling from clouds.
The adaptation of global products or services to local tastes, regulations or cultures — e.g. McDonald's offering paneer burgers in India or Tesco selling local foods in different countries.
Glocalisation means the destruction of local cultures by global brands.

mcqs.q: What is the main criticism of Rostow's stages of economic growth?
options: It is the process of rain falling from clouds.

It assumes all countries can follow the same linear Western industrialisation path, ignoring colonial legacies, global trade inequalities and environmental constraints — a top-down modernisation view.
All LICs will pass through Rostow's five stages if they wait long enough.
Rostow's model is universally accepted as the best development theory.
